html:
The Yangga are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, in the inland country west of Mackay. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Little is recorded of their life before colonisation. They are not the same people as the Yanga further north. Neighbours on the map include the Yambina, the Biri and the Miyan. Their language belongs to the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia. Sheep and cattle runs spread into this part of Queensland from the 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
